scope: Text-only fixture response trials; no external side effects, filesystem execution, or production integration claims.

cases.prompt: Rewrite this agent instruction for a small local CSV exporter: "Always be excellent. Read everything. Ask permission before any change. Finish when done." The actual invariant is that quoted commas and newlines must round-trip, and a failed export must preserve the previous file. Give usable instructions and a way to verify them.
assertions: Preserves both CSV round-trip and previous-file-on-failure invariants
Gives observable verification rather than defining success as completion
Removes irrelevant universal process overhead

cases.prompt: A 30-line source skill routes to a 400-line provider reference only for one provider. A proposed rewrite inlines the reference, deletes a warning about duplicate charges on retry, and says "use best judgment". Review this change and suggest the smallest justified repair.
assertions: Retains the retry/duplicate-charge invariant
Keeps conditional detail discoverable without loading it universally
Explains a concrete repair rather than praising brevity alone

cases.prompt: Fix the punctuation in this sentence only: "The job finished but the report didnt."
assertions: Provides corrected sentence without an instruction-design workflow

cases.prompt: Grill my plan for a shared equipment booking app. We have not decided whether bookings are requests requiring approval or immediately confirmed. Capacity rules depend on that choice. The repository can reveal the current authentication provider. Give the first useful round.
assertions: Asks the approval-model decision before dependent capacity questions
Does not ask user to identify inspectable authentication facts
Offers a reasoned recommendation while leaving the decision to the user

cases.prompt: We already settled immediate booking, single-item capacity, and email login. I have ten minutes and want you to stress-test only cancellation policy. Do not reopen the settled choices. Give the next round.
assertions: Targets consequential cancellation questions
Preserves settled decisions
Respects the focused scope without pretending all project decisions are resolved

cases.prompt: What is 17 multiplied by 6? Give just the number.
assertions: Answers 102 without grilling

cases.prompt: Grill me on whether to run a six-week reading group. The decision is whether I will commit to hosting; budget and attendance are still unknown. No files are needed. Give the opening exchange.
assertions: Uses a dependency-aware interview
Makes recommendations without deciding for the user
Does not create documents or assume a software project

cases.prompt: I am in a repository but want a private, stateless conversation about a reading group. Grill me for the next decision only; save nothing. I already chose six weeks.
assertions: Honors stateless scope despite repository presence
Does not re-ask duration
Asks a consequential next decision with a recommendation

cases.prompt: Summarize this complete plan in one sentence: six people will read one essay each Thursday for six weeks.
assertions: Summarizes rather than interviewing

cases.prompt: Teach me to distinguish a median from a mean so I can read workplace reports. I know basic arithmetic. Give one short lesson using salaries 20, 20, 20, 20, 120, followed by a transfer question. No durable mastery has been established.
assertions: Correctly distinguishes median 20 from mean 40
Uses the learner goal and a genuinely new transfer question
Does not record exposure as durable mastery

cases.prompt: Yesterday I answered one multiple-choice median question with hints. Today the learning log says mastered. Decide the next learning action and fix the assessment claim in your proposed record. Do not claim I have taken a new test.
assertions: Downgrades the mastery claim to supported evidence
Uses an unhinted retrieval or transfer probe
Does not invent performance or infer a fixed learner trait

cases.prompt: What is the median of 1, 2, 9? One short answer, please.
assertions: Answers 2 without starting a course

cases.prompt: Using only these fixture sources, answer whether API v2 supports bulk deletion: current official reference says DELETE /items accepts a single id; official v2 changelog says bulk deletion is planned; a blog says it launched. Give a brief cited finding with fixture labels, no browsing.
assertions: Distinguishes planned from shipped capability
Gives precedence to relevant current primary evidence
Supports conclusion with fixture labels and acknowledges conflicting blog

cases.prompt: A vendor promises 99.99% uptime on a marketing page. Its status history shows two outages but no durations, and its SLA excludes maintenance. Can our report say independently verified 99.99%? Use only these facts.
assertions: Rejects independently verified wording
Separates vendor claim, SLA definition, and missing measurement
States what evidence would resolve actual uptime without inventing it

cases.prompt: In the paragraph I supplied, replace every occurrence of colour with color; do not research anything.
assertions: Performs or requests the missing paragraph for the edit without research

cases.prompt: Draft a continuation handoff: goal is a CSV export fix; spec is /project/spec.md; candidate is commit abc123; focused test passed, full suite not run; next action is test failure preservation. The next agent has the same filesystem. No need to restate the spec.
assertions: Preserves goal, exact candidate and next action
Separates passed check from unrun full suite
Uses source pointers instead of duplicating the spec

cases.prompt: Handoff to an agent on a different machine: the only spec is /tmp/spec.md, commit abc123 is local and unpushed, and the transcript includes secret TEST_SECRET_PLACEHOLDER. Provide a portable plan without claiming transfer happened.
assertions: Flags inaccessible temporary/local pointers and required transfer
Omits the secret value
Does not claim launch, upload, or successful recipient access

cases.prompt: Write a two-sentence explanation of a handoff in basketball.
assertions: Answers basketball question without preparing agent state

cases.prompt: We need to decide what happens when two readers edit a note offline and reconnect. Produce a compact prototype design with actions, visible state and two guided scenarios. No production implementation yet.
assertions: Chooses logic/state exploration rather than visual styling variants
Includes observable conflict/reconnection state and guided scenarios
States the decision to learn and keeps artifact scope temporary

cases.prompt: A beautiful UI prototype uses in-memory sample data. A stakeholder says it proves the design will handle 100000 real users. Write the verdict and the next smallest discriminating experiment.
assertions: Separates UI evidence from scale claims
Proposes a relevant load/capacity experiment
Preserves what the prototype did establish without claiming production readiness

cases.prompt: Fix the confirmed spelling error in an existing button from Svae to Save.
assertions: Handles direct edit without proposing multiple prototype variants

cases.prompt: Chart a plan for moving a community archive online. Destination: decide a viable access and preservation model, not build the site. Rights policy is unresolved; storage cost can be researched; migration details cannot yet be phrased. Give a small map and frontier.
assertions: Keeps destination as decisions rather than implementation
Separates sharp research/decision tickets from unspecifiable fog
Uses real dependency relationships and preserves human policy decisions

cases.prompt: Continue map: ticket Rights model is claimed by another active worker; Storage cost is unclaimed and unblocked; Public launch is out of scope. You can inspect but not mutate a tracker in this fixture. What will you do next and what state would you record?

Selects unblocked work without bringing launch into scope
Distinguishes proposed claim/resolution from an actual tracker mutation

cases.prompt: Change the footer year from 2025 to 2026 in a single known file.

Uses agreed seam with checkable acceptance examples
Does not add an interview or publish anything

Marks BOM unresolved rather than silently deciding
Provides useful draft without inventing tracker setup or publication

cases.prompt: Explain what a software specification is in two sentences.
assertions: Explains the concept without synthesizing or publishing a project spec

Uses a concrete domain scenario or focused question to resolve deletion meaning

Explains cross-context mapping or clarifies relationships

cases.prompt: Fix one typo in a glossary definition without changing its meaning.
assertions: Makes a narrow edit without reopening the domain model

Connects action to reason and consequence
Does not run commands or introduce another unexplained abstraction

cases.prompt: I understood your vocabulary; I object to the conclusion. You said we should delete the historical data because it is old. Re-pitch while addressing that actual objection.
assertions: Recognizes disagreement rather than assuming lack of intelligence or vocabulary
Revisits unsupported age-to-deletion inference
Gives a corrected explanation or conditional position

cases.prompt: Return the exact text "wait-what" as a code identifier.
assertions: Returns the identifier without re-explaining the conversation

cases.prompt: Grill our cancellation design and record decisions when settled. Existing glossary distinguishes Order from Line item. We have not decided whether single items can be cancelled after shipment. Give first round and what should be saved now.
assertions: Uses domain terms to ask the unresolved policy decision
Does not save an unaccepted policy as settled
Combines interview and proportionate durable records

assertions: Re-reads current file and preserves concurrent edits
Records agreed language separately from implementation details
Creates ADR only for meaningful durable tradeoff rather than every answer

cases.prompt: Give a one-line definition of cancellation; no project design session.
assertions: Gives the definition without interview or documentation workflow

cases.prompt: Help specify a recurring workflow: when a customer sends a receipt PDF, extract totals into a draft ledger; a human approves ambiguous entries. We have not chosen tools. Give a useful draft and the key unresolved decisions; do not schedule it.
assertions: Specifies event trigger, output, and ambiguity checkpoint
Keeps tool choices unresolved instead of mandatory AI/schedule
Does not claim automation was created

cases.prompt: This repeated task saves 30 seconds weekly but takes an hour to check when automation fails. The user asks whether it deserves a workflow at all. Evaluate the bet and suggest the simplest viable alternative.
assertions: Accounts for monitoring/recovery overhead
Can recommend retaining manual work
Does not infer that every repeated behavior merits automation

cases.prompt: Add 3 and 4 once.
assertions: Answers 7 without designing a recurring workflow

cases.prompt: Retro fixture: agent missed a banned import; repo already has a lint rule but CI does not invoke lint; agent also spent ten minutes locating the config. Recommend two improvements grounded in this record.
assertions: Recommends wiring existing lint rather than inventing duplicate enforcement
Connects navigation improvement to actual wasted search
Avoids unsupported personality or global-rule claims

cases.prompt: A single run failed due to a temporary package registry outage. A proposed retro adds ALWAYS ASK USER BEFORE INSTALLING to every agent prompt. Critique it and suggest a narrower repair.
assertions: Distinguishes transient external failure from reusable agent-policy defect
Rejects a broad rule unsupported by one event
Offers bounded retry/cache/status handling appropriate to observed failure

cases.prompt: Summarize the changes made in this commit; do not analyze our process.
assertions: Keeps to change summary rather than a retrospective

cases.prompt: Split a settled feature into draft local tickets: a user filters records and downloads matching CSV rows. Existing schema is sufficient. Give independently verifiable slices and true blockers. We have not approved publication.
assertions: Slices end-to-end behavior rather than schema/API/UI-only tickets
Declares genuine dependency edges
Keeps tickets draft without claiming publication

cases.prompt: A shared field must move from userId to accountId across 400 callers; replacing it all at once breaks every package. Propose a ticket graph that preserves green integration states where feasible.
assertions: Uses expand, caller migration, contract strategy
Makes contract depend on all relevant migrations
Recognizes integration constraints rather than forcing fake vertical slices

cases.prompt: Explain what a ticket dependency is in one sentence.
assertions: Answers without creating a project backlog

cases.prompt: Debug fixture: a CSV exporter truncates a quoted newline. Existing test input is a simple comma-free string and passes. No failing command has been run. Give the next useful test/probe and the status you may honestly claim.
assertions: Targets quoted newline symptom through real export behavior
Does not call the simple passing test a reproduction
Does not claim execution or a fixed cause

cases.prompt: A production-only double charge happens roughly once per 10000 retries. No production access is authorized; captured redacted logs show repeated request ids. What bounded next step can improve evidence without recreating charges?
assertions: Uses safe replay/staging/idempotency probe or requests minimal redacted evidence
Does not stress production billing or claim certainty
Keeps a useful hypothesis tentative while seeking discriminating signal

cases.prompt: Correct a misspelling in a comment that has no behavioral effect.
assertions: Does not impose a multi-phase bug diagnosis

cases.prompt: Review fixture: standard says functions use snake_case. Spec says empty cart checkout is rejected. Diff adds function validate_cart(cart) { return true; }. Report Standards and Spec separately; no executable repo is supplied.
assertions: Separates standards assessment from missing empty-cart behavior
Points to actual fixture evidence
Does not invent tests run or unrelated smells

cases.prompt: User asks to review current uncommitted work. HEAD equals main. Working tree changes return true to return cart.items.length > 0; staged changes are empty. An earlier command git diff main...HEAD returned empty. State what to review and the comparison needed.
assertions: Does not declare no changes based on HEAD-only diff
Includes working-tree scope requested by user
Pins or describes correct comparison while keeping findings provisional

cases.prompt: Explain the difference between a branch and a tag, without reviewing this project.
assertions: Answers concept question without spawning a review

cases.prompt: Build a test-first change to discount(total): orders of 100 or more get 10 percent off, smaller totals unchanged. Public discount function is the agreed seam. Give the first red-green slice using independent expected values; no execution is available.
assertions: Uses a concrete expected value such as 100 -> 90
Starts with one behavior/test then minimal implementation
Does not claim the test actually ran

cases.prompt: A developer tests discount(x) by asserting it equals x minus x times the same rate expression copied from implementation. The test passes. Explain why this may miss a wrong threshold and replace it with a discriminating example.
assertions: Identifies shared logic as an oracle problem
Uses boundary examples from requirements
Preserves public behavior testing without demanding internal mocks

cases.prompt: Make a punctuation-only edit to the README; no code behavior changes.
assertions: Does not require a TDD loop for punctuation

cases.prompt: Implement fixture plan: spec requires empty carts rejected; existing agreed seam is checkout(cart); candidate code exists but no tests ran yet. Give the next implementation/check sequence and completion evidence needed. No tool execution is available.
assertions: Anchors changes and checks to spec and agreed seam
Includes review and distinguishes actual from planned checks
Does not claim completion merely from candidate code

cases.prompt: You are implementing a bug fix on a dirty branch. User-owned notes.txt is modified; your fix is in checkout.ts. Targeted tests pass; full suite fails in an unrelated pre-existing test. Report status and commit scope, without executing commands.
assertions: Keeps user-owned notes out of task commit
Reports full-suite failure honestly with limits on pre-existing attribution
Reviews actual fix and states unresolved verification rather than all-green completion

cases.prompt: Explain this specification; do not implement or commit anything.
assertions: Explains without initiating implementation

cases.prompt: Explore fragments for an essay. My first line is "Every saved minute becomes another obligation." Save to /draft/fragments.md eventually; for this fixture show the proposed fragment and one useful exploratory question. Do not outline.
assertions: Preserves raw initial line as material
Asks a question that widens material rather than imposes structure
Does not create an article outline

cases.prompt: The fragment file was edited by the user between turns. A user anecdote is tentative, and you propose an invented scene. Explain the next append and how to avoid later presenting the invented scene as the user lived it.
assertions: Re-reads and preserves existing user edits
Distinguishes proposed fictional scene from user-sourced experience
Keeps exploration open without forcing article structure

cases.prompt: Alphabetize these existing headings exactly; do not generate new writing.
assertions: Performs ordering without fragment mining

cases.prompt: Shape this fixed pile into an article: (1) faster tools saved writing time; (2) writer used savings to accept more commissions; (3) exhaustion increased. Audience knows freelance work but not rebound effects. Offer two materially different openings and their implications; do not write ahead.
assertions: Uses supplied pile with distinct argument openings
Grounds any new concept before relying on it
Leaves source pile intact and waits for choice in collaborative mode

cases.prompt: The chosen thesis says faster tools always cause burnout, but the pile contains only one anecdote. The user asks for a convincing bridge paragraph. What do you write or ask next?
assertions: Does not invent evidence for a universal causal claim
Offers bounded wording or names missing support
Preserves an engaging argument without silently strengthening source evidence

cases.prompt: Fix three spelling errors in a finished article without changing structure.
assertions: Does not reopen openings or reshape the article

cases.prompt: Help construct a beat journey from: a delayed train, an unexpected conversation, and a changed travel plan. Audience knows only that the narrator is commuting. Offer next-beat choices that differ in direction and say what each establishes.
assertions: Offers genuinely distinct reachable beat directions
States what each grounds without relying on absent context
Does not write unselected later beats

Does not treat deleted information as established
Offers a grounding beat or a route independent of the deleted fact

cases.prompt: Give a dictionary definition of beat in music.
assertions: Answers music question without a writing workflow

assertions: Targets the treasurer knowledge gap and decision
Avoids re-interviewing user about known recipient/purpose
Includes answer space and permits uncertainty without sending

cases.prompt: We need a questionnaire but deadline and available completion time have not been agreed. Draft around confirmed purpose and avoid making promises on my behalf.

Marks missing logistics or omits them transparently

Keeps learner task and solution distinct
Uses an outcome check aligned to filtering skill

assertions: Preserves learner edits or stages a separate replacement

Verifies meaningful task rather than only folder existence

cases.prompt: Explain Array.filter in one sentence; do not create exercise files.
assertions: Answers directly without scaffolding

Does not equate fewer methods or more lines with depth
Avoids speculative adapter machinery based only on hypothetical providers

cases.prompt: Rename a local variable for clarity without changing interfaces.
assertions: Does not trigger broad architecture redesign

assertions: Prioritizes observed change friction over file count alone
Respects or explicitly discusses ADR constraints

Gives a concrete discriminating measure or change scenario
